title: 10DS, i.AI, DSIT, and the new GDS: chronology with a refused succession

selection.selection_unit: One source-explicit central-government digital, data, or AI unit creation, transfer, merger, continuing identity, collaboration, or comparator event.
selection.selection_basis: Issue #32 exercised the smallest official chronology needed to test a proposed 10DS to i.AI to GDS/DSIT succession without assuming that similar remit or collaboration equals inheritance.
selection.denominator_description: The named UK units are bounded, but budgets, administrative status, leadership, personnel, programmes, supplier records, and matched comparator attributes have not been normalised across each year.
selection.target_removal_test: The institutional-succession question remains coherent without Electric Twin or any vendor.
selection.privacy_boundary: Official organisational, programme, staffing-target, accounting, recruitment, and collaboration records only.
promotion_blockers: budget and personnel transfer evidence remains incomplete
the official merger perimeter differs across current descriptions and requires source-by-source normalisation
the GSA comparator has not been normalised under the same institutional battery
the repository receipts are structured official-source extracts rather than complete remote-page snapshots

observations.factual_statement: An official No. 10 description states that the No. 10 Data Science team, 10DS, formed in mid-2020 with a remit to improve how key decisions are informed by data, analysis, and evidence and to promote evidence-informed policy across government.
observations.allowed_language: 10DS is documented as a No. 10 team formed in mid-2020 with a data-and-evidence decision remit.
forbidden_inferences: Formation of 10DS proves that it later became i.AI.
A similar remit proves transfer of staff, budget, assets, or mandate.
The team description establishes any vendor relationship.

observations.factual_statement: A government speech delivered on 20 November 2023 announced the Incubator for Artificial Intelligence, i.AI, as a new team with an initial target of thirty technical, programme, product, and engagement staff.
observations.allowed_language: i.AI was announced as a new government team in November 2023 with an initial staffing target.
forbidden_inferences: The announcement proves 10DS personnel, budget, or assets transferred into i.AI.
A staffing target proves actual headcount or later delivery.

observations.factual_statement: The 8 July 2024 machinery-of-government announcement states that experts in data, digital, and AI from GDS, CDDO, and i.AI would move from the Cabinet Office into DSIT to unite public-service digital-transformation efforts under one department.
objects: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
observations.allowed_language: An announced departmental transfer of named GDS, CDDO, and i.AI expertise into DSIT is documented.
forbidden_inferences: The announced transfer proves every employee, budget, contract, programme, or asset moved.
Departmental co-location proves institutional inheritance or common control beyond the official transfer.

observations.factual_statement: The DSIT accounting statement records GDS, CDDO, and i.AI transferring into DSIT during the 2024-25 period. Current official organisational descriptions state that CDDO, the Geospatial Commission, GDS, and i.AI merged to create the new GDS; the current GDS description also names the Responsible Technology Adoption Unit among the teams brought together in January 2025.
objects: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
observations.allowed_language: Official records document transfer into DSIT and the formation of a new GDS from several named predecessor teams, while the exact listed merger perimeter varies across official descriptions.
forbidden_inferences: A variable official merger perimeter may be flattened into one definitive list without source attribution.
Organisational merger proves continuity of every programme, person, budget, contract, or technical asset.

observations.factual_statement: The UK Government AI Playbook describes cyber-security experts from CDDO, Number 10DS, and i.AI collaborating through red-teaming on GOV.UK Chat.
observations.allowed_language: The three named teams collaborated on a red-teaming activity.
forbidden_inferences: Collaboration proves succession, merger, personnel transfer, or shared budget.
Participation in one project establishes organisational identity.

observations.factual_statement: Across the bounded official chronology opened for this case, no source states that 10DS became i.AI, transferred its staff or budget to i.AI, or merged into the new GDS. The sources instead separately document 10DS formation, i.AI creation, collaboration among 10DS, CDDO, and i.AI, and the later transfer and merger of named GDS, CDDO, i.AI, Geospatial, and responsible-technology teams.
observations.query_scope: Named official formation, transfer, merger, organisational-description, accounting, and collaboration records opened for issue #32 through 21 July 2026.
observations.allowed_language: The proposed 10DS to i.AI succession is not established by the opened official sources and remains a hypothesis.
forbidden_inferences: The bounded null proves no personnel, knowledge, or informal continuity existed.
Failure to find a source-explicit transfer proves institutional independence in every respect.
The search can be generalized beyond its named sources and date.

observations.factual_statement: The US General Services Administration states that its Centers of Excellence were established in October 2017 and included artificial intelligence among several cross-agency modernisation capabilities delivered through federal and private-sector participation.
observations.allowed_language: GSA Centers of Excellence is a plausible comparator candidate for a government AI-capability unit battery.
forbidden_inferences: The GSA programme is already matched to 10DS, i.AI, or GDS on mandate, budget, staffing, or legal status.
Similarity in broad AI-modernisation purpose establishes institutional equivalence.

case_disposition.machine_summary: Official records now have immutable repository source extracts for separate unit creation, a named transfer into DSIT, formation of the new GDS, collaboration, the bounded succession refusal, and a comparator candidate. They do not establish 10DS as a predecessor of i.AI or the new GDS. Human review and institutional/comparator normalisation remain incomplete.

interpretation_contract.what_this_is: A receipted bounded institutional chronology with source-explicit creations, transfer, merger, collaboration, a refused succession, and an unnormalised comparator candidate.
interpretation_contract.what_this_is_not: Proof that 10DS became i.AI, proof of personnel or budget transfer, a complete institutional genealogy, a vendor pathway, a full remote-page archive, or a promoted thesis evidence packet.
interpretation_contract.copy_ready_caveat: Official records document 10DS and i.AI as separately created teams and later document the transfer and merger of named digital and AI bodies into DSIT and the new GDS. No opened source establishes that 10DS became i.AI or merged into the new GDS; collaboration and similar remit are not institutional inheritance.
